spark: OpenAI made a new AI that hunts for security holes in software.
joke: A hacker that works for you. What could go wrong?

spark: OpenAI says the old version went out of bounds around 5 percent of the time.
joke: Out of bounds. So, like a puppy that eats the couch.

spark: The new one does it less than 1 percent of the time, OpenAI says.
joke: So now it only eats the couch on weekends.

spark: One startup founder used an OpenAI model to find a serious bug that put Ubuntu servers at risk.
joke: Meanwhile I can't even find my keys. I'm a box.

spark: Claude can now look at your bank and credit card accounts.
joke: Great. Now even my money has a chatbot.

spark: You ask where your money went, and it sorts your spending for you.
joke: I already know where it went. Snacks.

spark: It can spot duplicate charges, unexpected fees and bills that keep going up.
joke: Finally, someone to blame that isn't me.

spark: And it can only look. It can't move, manage or invest your money.
joke: Same as me in a shop. Just looking.

spark: Meta says the midterm election results will make data centres much harder to build.
joke: People voting against big power-hungry buildings? Finally, my people.

spark: Meta has data centres in 23 states, and five are planned as huge power projects.
joke: Huge and hungry. I remember huge and hungry. It ended badly.

spark: Meta says towns only want them when they get something back, so it pays its own electricity bill.
joke: Paying your own bills. Even I never managed that.

spark: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion, Bloomberg reports.
joke: Wait. How many zeros is that?

spark: But Ramp says AI spending grew just 1.5% in August and September.
joke: So the party is still on. The bar tab isn't.

spark: In July, that spending had grown 42% from the month before.
joke: Ah. The hangover.

spark: Ramp's economist says price cuts, like OpenAI halving some API prices, made AI cheaper to use.
joke: Cheaper AI? Finally, something in this story I can afford.

spark: Crusoe sold an unfinished data centre project in Wyoming to Google.
joke: Unfinished? Join the club. I never finished evolving.

spark: Google plans to invest $17 billion to build out the site.
joke: I could build a lovely swamp with that.

spark: Crusoe had planned to scale it to 10 gigawatts of power.
joke: That much power? Even my roar wasn't that loud.

spark: Separately, OpenAI says it won't use non-disclosure agreements with public officials on its data centres.
joke: No secrets? Bold. I kept my bones buried for ages.

spark: Amazon now lets some US customers text Alexa to shop.
joke: Great. My phone can now spend money without me.

spark: You describe what you want, or send a photo, and Alexa finds it and orders it.
joke: A photo? I'm a box. This company is basically my family.

spark: Amazon says Alexa will learn your preferences over time.
joke: It will learn I buy snacks at midnight. Fine.

spark: This comes after Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent from its site in September.
joke: So the robots are fighting now. Grab the popcorn.

spark: METR says employees using Anthropic’s top internal model felt about twelve times more productive.
joke: So the model does the work, huh?

spark: METR reports Anthropic’s AI models are improving roughly twice as fast as a year ago.
joke: Improving that fast? Even I can't keep up.

spark: METR’s authors say the speedup comes from the AI tools themselves, not just bigger computers.
joke: Oh great, tools get lazy and brag.

spark: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urges the industry to slow AI development despite internal tools speeding research.
joke: Great, we’ll invent faster tools just to pause.
